Check the category table below for men and women ranges.

How accurate is the U.S. Navy formula? When measured carefully, its error is typically around 3-4% compared with laboratory methods such as hydrostatic weighing. Keep measurements consistent and not too tight for the best result.

What do the ACE categories mean? They follow the American Council on Exercise ranges: essential fat, athletes, fitness, average and obese. They are general guides and your ideal range depends on age, sport and personal goals.

Why is the hip measurement only for women? Women store proportionally more fat around the hips and thighs, so the formula uses waist plus hip minus neck for them. Men can be estimated from the waist alone.

body-fat-calculator.p: Different formulas use different measurements — neck, waist, hip and height — and each returns slightly different results. Treat the output as a consistent trend marker from the same method, not an absolute lab measurement.

list: Very low ranges suit athletes but often come with health trade-offs.
Mid ranges (roughly 15–25% men, 20–32% women) are common healthy zones.
Consistent weekly measurement beats a single anxious reading.
Hydration and time of day shift results by a few percent.

ideal-weight-calculator.p: This free calculator reports the two most common ideal weight formulas. Devine gives 50 + 2.3 × (height in inches - 60) for men and 45.5 + 2.3 × (height in inches - 60) for women. Robinson gives 52 + 1.9 × (...) for men and 49 + 1.7 × (...) for women. It also shows the healthy range for a BMI between 18.5 and 24.9.

list: Select your sex and enter your height in centimeters.
Optional: enter your current weight to compare it with the healthy range.
Read the Devine and Robinson ideal weight values.
See the healthy BMI weight range and a color hint for your position in it.

Which ideal weight should I trust? The formulas were built for height-based estimates on adult populations, so small differences between them are normal. The healthy BMI range is often the better practical target because it acknowledges a span of healthy weights.

Why do men and women get different values? On average women have less lean mass and more essential body fat at the same height, so both formulas start from a lower base for women (45.5-49 kg instead of 50-52 kg) and the Robinson slope is smaller.
What is the healthy BMI range? A BMI between 18.5 and 24.9 is considered normal weight by the WHO. The calculator converts that BMI range to a weight range in kilograms based on your height.

ideal-weight-calculator.p: Devine, Robinson and Miller each make different assumptions about body build, so the 'ideal' number varies by a few kilos between them. The variation is normal — the tool shows a range so you do not fixate on one magic digit.

Body composition means two people of the same height and weight can have very different health pictures. Use the result as a rough reference zone alongside the BMI tool, and let a clinician apply judgement for anything medically meaningful.

sleep-calculator.h: How does the sleep calculator work?
sleep-calculator.p: A full sleep cycle lasts about 90 minutes and goes through light sleep, deep sleep and REM sleep. This free calculator adds about 15 minutes for falling asleep and then works backwards from your wake-up time — or forwards from your bedtime — to recommend schedules that end at the natural end of the 5th or 6th cycle.

list: Choose the wake-up mode to get recommended bedtimes, or the bedtime mode for wake-up suggestions.
Pick a time with the time input.
Read the suggestions for 5 and 6 sleep cycles.
Copy the full list with one click and follow the schedule that fits your life.

Why are 5 or 6 cycles recommended? Waking up inside deep sleep makes you groggy, while waking between cycles leaves you more alert. With 5 cycles you sleep about 7.5 hours and with 6 about 9 hours, plus roughly 15 minutes to fall asleep.

Do I have to start in bed exactly at the suggested time? No. The suggested bedtime is when you should aim to fall asleep about 15 minutes later. Falling asleep a few minutes off is fine — consistency matters more than a perfect minute.

Can I use it if I sleep less than 5 cycles? It works with any wake-up or bedtime you enter. Staying within complete cycles is ideal, but a 4-cycle night is still calculated correctly if that is what your schedule allows.

sleep-calculator.p: Sleep runs in roughly 90-minute cycles of light, deep and REM stages. Waking mid-cycle leaves you groggy, while aligning alarms to cycle boundaries — about 5 or 6 cycles for a night — feels dramatically more rested with the same total sleep.

A fixed bedtime and wake time train your internal clock, which usually matters more than chasing an extra 15 minutes. If you must cut sleep for a night, keep the pattern stable the rest of the week instead of scheduling wildly different hours.

cron-tester.h: What is a Cron Expression Tester?
cron-tester.p: A Cron Expression Tester checks a five-field cron expression such as 0 9 * * MON-FRI and explains what each field matches in plain language. It then scans forward minute by minute from now to find the next five exact run times, which you can copy as ISO-style or localized timestamps.

cron-tester.h: How do the five fields work?
list: Minute (0–59): picks the minute of each hour; */5 matches every 5 minutes.
Hour (0–23): selects which hours run; 9-17 means 09:00 through 17:00.
Day of month (1–31): selects days such as 1,15,31 or a range like 1-15.
Month (1–12 or JAN–DEC): restricts the expression to certain months; names like JAN-DEC are accepted.
Day of week (0–7 or SUN–SAT): 0 and 7 both mean Sunday; MON-FRI matches weekdays.
What syntax does the tool accept? Standard five-field cron syntax: *, */n, a-b, a-b/n and comma-separated lists like 0,15,30,45.
Are month and weekday names case-sensitive? No — MON, mon and Mon are all accepted and can be mixed freely with numbers.
Do day-of-month and day-of-week combine? Yes, like classic cron: when both are restricted, a date matches when either field matches.
The five fields are minute, hour, day-of-month, month and day-of-week.
* means 'every' — * * * * * runs every minute.
Lists, ranges and steps: 0,15,30,45; 9-17; */30.
A known gotcha: a strict day-of-month and day-of-week can conflict, depending on the engine.

cron-tester.p: Cron interprets time in the server's time zone, not yours. A job tuned against your calendar can fire hours off from what you expected after a server moves regions or daylight saving changes — the tester shows the resulting instants so the mismatch is obvious.

aes-encryption.p: This tool encrypts your text with AES-GCM 256, a modern authenticated cipher, using a key derived from your password with PBKDF2 (100,000 iterations). The same password can decrypt the stored value back, and everything runs in your browser with nothing uploaded.

aes-encryption.h: Why is the output in three parts?
list: Salt: random bytes that make the derived key unique even for the same password.
IV: a fresh random initialization vector generated for every encryption.
Ciphertext: the encrypted bytes plus an integrity tag so tampering is always detected.
All three are base64-encoded and joined as base64(salt).base64(iv).base64(ciphertext); decrypt parses this exact format.
Can you decrypt my data? No — the password is required to derive the key, and encryption happens entirely in the browser; the tool never sees your plaintext or password.
Why is it not instant? PBKDF2 runs 100,000 iterations on purpose to make brute-force attacks expensive; that delay is what keeps the encryption strong.
A decrypt error says wrong password or bad format — what now? Either the password does not match, the value was edited, or the three base64 parts are missing.

aes-encryption.p: AES is a symmetric cipher: the same key encrypts and decrypts. It is the encryption standard behind TLS and disk encryption, and its security rests entirely on keeping the key secret — lose it and the data is unrecoverable by anyone.

list: Key length (128/192/256) affects strength; 256 is the common safe choice.
The IV (initialization vector) randomizes output so identical inputs encrypt differently.
Mode chains blocks: CBC and GCM are widespread, GCM adds authentication.
Reusing an IV with the same key leaks information — never do it.

random-string-generator.h: What is a Random String Generator?
random-string-generator.p: A Random String Generator instantly produces random text from the character types you enable: uppercase, lowercase, digits and symbols. It uses the browser crypto.getRandomValues API with unbiased sampling, so results suit tokens, salts, one-time codes and test data.

list: Uppercase (A–Z): capital letters.
Lowercase (a–z): lower-case letters.
Digits (0–9): numbers.
Symbols (!@#$…): punctuation and special characters.
Length: any value from 1 to 128 characters; you can regenerate as many times as you like.
Is it really random? Yes — values come from crypto.getRandomValues, a cryptographic-quality source; every generation is fresh and independent.
Can the same string appear twice? Randomness means a repeat is technically possible, but with long strings the chance is astronomically small.
Is the result stored or uploaded? No — generation happens locally in your browser and nothing is sent to any server.

random-string-generator.h: What to use random strings for
list: Password salts and reset tokens that must never repeat.
Temporary identifiers for test data and fixtures.
Example keys in documentation and demos.
Unique name suffixes when copy-pasting between environments.

random-string-generator.p: Longer strings with a bigger alphabet give far more combinations. For security-critical values like salts or tokens, prefer 32+ characters from the full character set. For display or test purposes, shorter strings are fine and easier to type.

jwt-generator.p: A JWT Generator builds a signed JSON Web Token from three parts you control: a header that declares the signing algorithm, a payload with your claims, and a secret. The token is formed as header.payload.signature, where the signature proves the first two parts have not been altered since signing.

list: Header: small JSON declaring the algorithm (for example HS256), base64url-encoded without padding.
Payload: the claims — JSON such as issuer, subject and expiry, also base64url-encoded.
Signature: the HMAC-SHA256 digest of header.payload, keyed with your secret.
The final token is header.payload.signature, ready to copy into a test, curl command or another service.

jwt-generator.h: What role does the secret play?
jwt-generator.p: The secret is the private key that signs the token. The server that issues and verifies the token keeps the same secret. Anyone with the secret can forge tokens, so treat it like a password — never put it in client-side code or a public repository.

jwt-generator.h: When should you use a JWT?
list: Stateless authentication: the server verifies a signature instead of storing sessions.
API access: short-lived access tokens in Authorization headers.
Single sign-on between applications that share a signing secret.
Remember: JWTs are signed, not encrypted — never put passwords or personal data in the payload unless you add an extra layer of encryption.

jwt-generator.h: How to use the FreetoolsY generator
jwt-generator.p: Paste your header and payload JSON, type your secret and press generate. You get the complete token plus the three parts shown separately, with a copy button for the result. Everything is signed in your browser with the Web Crypto API — no part of the token or your secret ever leaves the page.

currency-converter.p: A Currency Converter converts an amount from one currency to another using reference rates you can adjust. It is useful for travel budgets, online shopping in foreign stores, freelance invoices and checking prices when an amount is quoted in another money.

currency-converter.h: Where do the rates come from?
currency-converter.p: The tool ships with fixed reference rates that you can override manually with the latest rate you know. Because markets change every second, double-check your figures against the spot rate when the exact amount matters.

list: Choose the source and target currencies.
Enter the amount or adjust the reference rate if yours differs.
Read the converted result and the reverse rate in one glance.
Can I update the rate? Yes — edit the base rate field before converting.
Do I need an internet connection? No, everything runs in your browser.
Is the exchange rate live? The initial values are reference rates; update them for the current market value.

compound-interest-calculator.p: Compound interest means your returns earn their own returns. This calculator shows how an initial deposit grows over the years when interest is added, with optional monthly contributions and a full yearly breakdown.

list: Starting amount and monthly deposit.
Annual rate and compounding frequency (yearly, monthly, daily).
Investment length in years or months.

compound-interest-calculator.p: The yearly breakdown shows exactly how much comes from contributions and how much is earned interest each year. Use it to compare scenarios, such as saving more each month versus getting a higher rate.

list: How does compounding frequency change? Pick daily, monthly or yearly in the settings and the table recalculates.
Is this tax-adjusted? No — the result is gross growth before any taxes or fees.
Is my data safe? All calculations happen in your browser; nothing is sent anywhere.

salary-calculator.h: What is a Net Salary Calculator?
salary-calculator.p: A Net Salary Calculator estimates how much of your gross wage you take home after SGK, unemployment insurance and income tax deductions. It follows Turkey's payroll system and gives you monthly and annual summaries.

list: Gross-to-net conversion with SGK and unemployment deductions.
Income tax according to the progressive brackets and the minimum wage deduction threshold.
Monthly, annual and per-pay-period breakdowns.

salary-calculator.p: Enter your gross wage and see the net salary instantly. Compare offers or check how a raise changes your take-home amount before you sign anything.

list: Is this number exact? It is an estimate; the final figure depends on your exact situation and employer choices.
Does it include bonuses? Overtime, bonuses and other perks are not covered.
Are tax brackets up to date? The calculator uses the current bracket logic; verify against the latest official rates.

sql-formatter.p: A SQL Formatter turns messy SQL into clean, readable queries — or compresses it into one compact line. Choose your indentation and keyword casing and format instantly in your browser.

list: Debugging long stored procedures with consistent alignment.
Sharing readable queries with teammates.
Preparing compact SQL for blog posts, chat or small tool windows.

sql-formatter.p: Pick the number of indent spaces and whether keywords are uppercase, lowercase or left as written. The Minify option strips whitespace for a single-line output.

list: Does it work for SQL Server, MySQL and Postgres? Yes — the formatter is generic and handles the common dialects.
Is my query sent to a server? No, everything runs locally in your browser.
Can I format without changing the query logic? Yes, formatting only changes whitespace and casing.

json-xml-converter.h: What is a JSON to XML Converter?
json-xml-converter.p: A JSON to XML Converter changes JSON data into XML and XML into JSON, in both directions. Arrays are preserved as repeated elements and XML attributes are supported, so most real-world documents convert cleanly.

list: Paste JSON or XML on the left, choose the direction and click Convert.
Review the output and the error message if conversion fails.
Copy the result with one click.

json-xml-converter.p: Documents with attributes round-trip using an @attr convention, and repeated elements become arrays. If a document is invalid, the tool points to the problem so you can fix it and convert again.

list: Is my data stored? No — everything is processed in your browser.
Does it keep the order of attributes? Attribute order is preserved when converting back.
Can I convert very large files? Yes, the conversion runs directly in your browser with no size limit.

markdown-html-converter.h: What is a Markdown to HTML Converter?
markdown-html-converter.p: A Markdown to HTML Converter writes HTML from Markdown or translates HTML back into Markdown, with a live preview so you see the result as you go.

list: Turning Markdown notes into HTML for emails or website editors.
Converting existing HTML pages back into clean Markdown.
Checking how a snippet will render before publishing.

markdown-html-converter.p: Yes. The conversion happens entirely in your browser, so pasted content never leaves your device — safe for drafts and internal documents.

list: Which Markdown is supported? Common syntax: headings, lists, code, tables and links.
Does HTML-to-Markdown handle complex layouts? It converts standard formatting; very complex nested markup may stay partly as HTML.
Do I need internet? No, the tool works offline in your browser.

hmac-generator.p: An HMAC Generator computes an HMAC-SHA256 or HMAC-SHA512 signature for your message using a secret key, and shows the result in hex and Base64. It is commonly used to verify the integrity and origin of API requests.

list: Paste your message text and your secret key.
Choose SHA-256 or SHA-512 as the hash function.
Copy the resulting signature in hex or Base64.

hmac-generator.p: The signature depends on the exact bytes of your message. Use the same signing settings as the service you are talking to, and never paste production secrets on untrusted machines — this tool runs entirely in your browser.

list: Is HMAC the same as simple hashing? No — HMAC keys the hash with a secret, so it proves authenticity, not just integrity.
Does it work on files? Not directly; hash the file contents first, then sign the hash.
Is my secret key safe? The key is processed locally in your browser and never transmitted.

html-table-generator.h: What is an HTML Table Generator?
html-table-generator.p: An HTML Table Generator creates ready-to-paste HTML table code from your rows, columns and pasted data, with a live preview so you see the final look before copying.

list: Set a blank grid with your chosen number of rows and columns.
Paste TSV data (for example, from Excel or Google Sheets).
Add a table caption and optional borders.

html-table-generator.p: Hand-writing table markup is tedious. This tool generates clean, ready-to-paste code you can drop into a CMS, editor or email template, then restyle with your own CSS.

list: Can I include a header row? Yes, the first row can be marked as table headers.
Does it support merged cells? Not automatically; the generator covers the common flat tables.
Where is the code produced? In your browser — nothing is uploaded.

favicon-generator.p: A Favicon Generator draws a favicon from a letter or short text plus your colors, then lets you download it as PNG or ICO. Use it to give a site a recognizable browser-tab icon without a graphics program.

list: Type the character or text you want on the icon and choose the text color.
Pick the background color (optionally with rounded corners).
Download as PNG or ICO and point your head at it.

favicon-generator.p: Favicons are tiny — keep the text short and the colors high-contrast. Test it in both light and dark tabs so the icon stays visible.

list: What is the difference between ICO and PNG? ICO keeps multiple sizes for older browsers; PNG is simpler and supported by modern ones.
Does it read my logo file? The generator draws from text; use an image editor for a custom logo.
Is my data private? Everything is generated client-side.

image-crop.p: An Image Cropper lets you trim any image to the exact area you want by dragging a selection box directly in the browser — no uploads, no signup.

list: Drop or select an image file.
Choose an aspect-ratio preset and drag over the area you want to keep.
Optionally rotate, flip, or zoom the preview; choose an output format and quality.
Download the cropped image as PNG, JPEG, or WebP.

image-crop.p: The preview is scaled only for display on large images. Cropping uses the selected area at the source resolution, while JPEG and WebP quality can be adjusted before export.

list: Can I set an exact pixel size? Crop visually first, then optionally resize the result with the site's image resizer.
Can I lock the crop to a preset ratio? Yes, choose a square, portrait, story, landscape, classic, or photo ratio before selecting the area.
What formats can I export? PNG, JPEG, and WebP. Quality can be adjusted for JPEG and WebP.
Is my photo uploaded? No — all processing happens locally in your browser.

image-watermark.p: An Image Watermark places a logo or image stamp over your photo at the position and opacity you choose, protecting your content or showing ownership on social shares.

list: Load the base image and the watermark image (a logo or signature).
Set the position, size and opacity.
Download the resulting image as PNG.

image-watermark.p: Lower opacity and a corner position keep photos clean while still identifying the source. Export as PNG so the composite keeps a transparent background where needed.

list: Can I add text instead of a logo? Use this tool with the watermark saved as an image, or use a dedicated text tool.
Does it resize the original? The output size follows the original image.
Is my content uploaded? No, everything runs in your browser.

jsonld-generator.p: A JSON-LD Generator builds schema.org structured data for common types — Article, Product, FAQPage, Event, Person and more — ready to paste into your page head for rich results.

list: Pick a structured data type.
Fill in the fields shown in plain language.
Copy the generated JSON-LD and paste it inside a script tag in your head.

jsonld-generator.p: Structured data helps search engines understand your content and can unlock rich results such as star ratings, FAQs and event listings — a small snippet with real visibility payoff.

list: Do I need to be a developer? No — the fields are labeled in plain language.
Does it produce valid JSON? Yes, the output is always valid JSON; verify it in Google's result-testing tools.
Where does processing happen? In your browser, so your content stays private.

hreflang-generator.p: An Hreflang Generator creates hreflang link tags and x-default entries for multilingual sites, then formats them for your head or your XML sitemap — no more hand-typing URL lists.

list: Enter the URL of each language version of the page.
Choose the output format: HTML link tags or sitemap-XML blocks.
Copy the output and paste it into your head or sitemap.

hreflang-generator.p: Every language version should list all of its siblings and add a matching x-default. The generator includes x-default so search engines see a complete, self-consistent signal.

list: Do I need hreflang on every page? Add it to every localized URL and mirror the tags on each version.
Do you validate the URLs? The tool formats the entries; verify the final code in Search Console.
Is my URL list uploaded? No, it is built locally in your browser.

robots-txt-generator.p: A Robots.txt Generator writes robots.txt content from presets — like allow-all or block-all — plus your own allow and disallow rules, ready to drop into your site root.

list: Start from a preset (allow all, block all, or block search crawlers).
Add specific paths to allow or disallow for each user agent.
Copy the final text into your /robots.txt file.

robots-txt-generator.p: robots.txt steers well-behaved crawlers; it is not a security barrier. Keep disallow rules to paths that should stay out of search results, and test changes in Search Console afterwards.

list: Which hostname should I use? Place one robots.txt at the root of the exact host you serve.
Can it point to a sitemap? Yes — the generated text includes a sitemap line.
Is the file stored anywhere? No, it is produced locally in your browser.

wheel-of-names.h: What is a Wheel of Names?
wheel-of-names.p: A Wheel of Names spins a colorful wheel carrying your list of names, then lands on a random winner. Perfect for classroom picks, prize draws, team assignments and friendly raffles.

list: Add each entry as a line in the names box.
Spin the wheel and watch it settle on a winner.
Remove the winner and spin again for a second prize.

wheel-of-names.h: Draws that are fair and fun
wheel-of-names.p: The spin is random, so the result is impartial — and the colorful wheel looks great on a projector or big screen while the tension builds.

list: Can I use pictures instead of names? The wheel supports text entries.
Can I pick several winners? Yes — remove a winner from the list and spin again.
Does it need internet? No, it runs entirely in your browser.

random-number-generator.h: What is a Random Number Generator?
random-number-generator.p: A Random Number Generator produces random numbers within any range you choose, with or without repeats. It is handy for lottery picks, sample selection, dice-like rolls and testing.

list: Enter the minimum and maximum of the range.
Choose how many numbers you want and whether repeats are allowed.
Generate, then copy the list or sort it.

random-number-generator.h: True randomness lives in the browser
random-number-generator.p: The generator uses the browser's cryptographic randomness source, so every draw is independent and cannot be predicted.

list: Can repeats be disabled? Yes — switch to unique-only mode when each number may appear once.
Does it support negative numbers? Yes, choose any range.
Is the result stored? No, numbers are generated locally.

stopwatch-timer.h: What is a Stopwatch and Timer?
stopwatch-timer.p: A Stopwatch measures elapsed time with lap splits, while a Timer counts down from a set duration and rings when finished. Two tools for timing craft, cooking, workouts and games.

list: Stopwatch: tap Start, record laps, and read the total and split times.
Timer: set minutes and seconds, then press Start.
Reset clears the current mode; the timer beeps when it finishes.

stopwatch-timer.p: Times are based on real clock time, so even if the tab is hidden the durations stay correct.

list: Can I record laps? Yes — as many as you need, kept in a scrollable list with splits and totals.
Does it ring on completion? The timer plays a short beep at zero.
Is anything transmitted? No — everything runs locally in your browser.

qr-code-reader.h: What is a QR code reader?
qr-code-reader.p: A QR code reader decodes the patterns printed on a QR square and turns them into readable content. Depending on the code, that content can be a website address, plain text, Wi-Fi settings, contact details or a payment reference.

qr-code-reader.h: How does reading an image work?
list: The image is rendered on a hidden canvas in your browser.
jsQR inspects the position markers and the black-and-white matrix.
The captured data is decoded from the pattern.
The result is shown as text you can copy.

qr-code-reader.h: When do you need to read a QR code from an image?
list: Recovering a link from an old screenshot.
Opening a printed code that you cannot scan live.
Verifying what a code contains before trusting it.
Forwarding the raw value of a code to someone else.

qr-code-reader.p: The image is processed with JavaScript on your device and never uploaded. Codes sometimes contain payment or login data, so keeping the process local protects you even when the payload itself is sensitive.

Crop closely around the QR square, keep the image sharp and make sure the code is flat in the frame. A little blur or a steep angle is the most common reason a read fails; when it does, nothing is sent anywhere, so you can simply try a better picture.

text-extractor.p: A text extractor scans a block of text and separates the structured pieces from the words around them — emails, phone numbers, URLs and hashtags. Instead of scrolling through a long message looking for every address or link, you get a clean, deduplicated list.

list: Email addresses such as name@example.com.
Phone numbers in common international formats.
Website links starting with http://, https:// or www.
Hashtags used on social media platforms.

text-extractor.p: The tool scans the text with regular expressions tuned for each type and removes duplicates automatically. Results follow the order of the text, so the first occurrence appears first. You can copy the whole list or a single value with one click.

list: Cleaning a customer list that mixes contacts and notes.
Collecting links shared in a long chat conversation.
Pulling every email out of a support ticket.
Building hashtag lists from a caption or comment thread.

text-extractor.p: No. All matching happens in your browser with JavaScript, so the text you paste is never uploaded or stored. For the phone-number filter, formats follow a common international pattern; dial extensions and unusual separators may be skipped.

css-gradient-generator.p: A CSS gradient is a smooth transition between two or more colors that the browser draws instead of loading an image file. The linear-gradient() function renders it as a straight color blend controlled by an angle and a set of color stops.

css-gradient-generator.h: How do the controls map to CSS?
css-gradient-generator.p: The angle slider writes the first argument of linear-gradient(). The first color starts at 0%, the last one finishes at 100%, and when a third color is enabled it becomes a stop in the middle whose position you can slide between 0% and 100%. The preset buttons simply pick common angles for you.

css-gradient-generator.h: When should I use a gradient?
list: Buttons, cards and hero backgrounds that need a modern look without an image.
Subtle depth on headers and sidebar items.
Placeholders and empty-state sections with no image asset.
Brand color transitions across banner areas.

css-gradient-generator.h: Why do gradients load faster than images?
css-gradient-generator.p: A gradient is pure CSS, so it adds no HTTP request and no file size. It scales to any resolution, stays crisp on high-DPI screens and adapts to the container size instantly — ideal for responsive layouts.

css-gradient-generator.h: Is the generated code ready to use?
css-gradient-generator.p: Yes. The output is a single standard background property. Paste it into your stylesheet and it works in every modern browser, since linear-gradient() no longer needs a vendor prefix.

border-radius-generator.p: border-radius rounds the corners of an element. Instead of applying a uniform radius, CSS lets you define up to four values — one per corner — so a box can look nearly square on one side and fully rounded on the other.

border-radius-generator.h: How do the four values work?
border-radius-generator.p: The order is clockwise starting from the top-left corner: top-left, top-right, bottom-right, bottom-left. When every corner shares the same value, the shorthand border-radius: 20px is enough; otherwise all four values are written in order.

border-radius-generator.h: What can rounded corners be used for?
list: Buttons, chips and badges with a soft pill look.
Cards and modals that feel friendlier than sharp rectangles.
Avatars that need a perfect circle by setting half the size.
Input fields and tags with a consistent radius.

border-radius-generator.h: Should the radius be small or large?
border-radius-generator.p: Small radii (2–8px) look subtle and professional; large radii (16–40px) feel rounded and playful. As a rule of thumb, keep the radius clearly smaller than the element — a radius larger than half the box simply produces a pill shape.
Yes. When the corners are linked, the tool writes the short form with a single value. As soon as any corner differs, it switches to four explicit values, so the output stays minimal and readable.

text-to-speech.p: Text to speech converts written words into spoken audio using synthetic voices. The browser reads the text out loud using a locally installed voice, so no files are uploaded to a server and nothing is stored.
Type or paste your text into the box, choose a voice from the list, and optionally adjust the speed and pitch sliders. Press Speak to hear it and Stop to pause the reading.

list: The list shows every voice installed on your device or provided by your operating system.
Voices vary by language; pick one that matches your text for the best pronunciation.
Some systems download extra voices from the browser's settings page.
Proofreading written content by ear to catch awkward phrasing.
Listening to articles, notes and study material on your device.
Practicing pronunciation in a foreign language.
Accessibility for people who prefer listening over reading.

text-to-speech.p: Yes. Speech synthesis runs entirely on your device through the browser's built-in engine. Your text is never sent to a server, and no account is required.

pomodoro-timer.p: The Pomodoro technique splits work into focused intervals, traditionally 25 minutes, separated by short breaks. Each completed interval is called a pomodoro. Working in blocks keeps concentration high and prevents burnout.

Set the work and break minutes you want, then press Start. The timer counts down each phase, plays a short beep when one ends, and moves automatically to the next one. Completed focus sessions are counted on the screen.

list: The classic cycle: 25 minutes work, 5 minutes break.
A longer rhythm: 45 minutes work, 15 minutes break, for deep tasks.
A sprint: 15 minutes work, 5 minutes break, for shallow or tiring chores.

pomodoro-timer.p: Stepping away briefly lets your brain consolidate what you learned and return refreshed. Regular small breaks reduce fatigue, making it easier to keep a steady pace for the whole day.
No. Countdown and the sound signal run entirely in your browser. Close the page and the cycle stops, but as long as the tab stays open the timer is accurate.

binary-text-converter.p: Binary code is the base-2 number system that uses only two digits, 0 and 1. Computers store every character, image and file as long sequences of these bits, and text is encoded into bytes first.

This tool encodes your text as UTF-8 bytes, the same encoding used on the web. Each byte is written as 8 bits, so the letter A becomes 01000001 and a Turkish or emoji character becomes several bytes joined together.

binary-text-converter.h: How do I decode binary back to text?
binary-text-converter.p: Paste the binary groups separated by spaces, switch the direction to Binary to Text and press Convert. Each 8-bit group is decoded as one byte and the bytes are joined back into the original message.

list: Learning how computers represent data at the lowest level.
Explaining encoding and bit patterns in lessons and presentations.
Creating hidden text messages or playful codes between friends.

binary-text-converter.p: Yes. Because the tool uses UTF-8 encoding, Turkish characters, Greek, Arabic and emoji all convert correctly and translate back without losing any information.

credit-card-validator.p: Card numbers are checked with the Luhn algorithm, a checksum formula. Starting from the right, every second digit is doubled, values above nine are reduced, and the total must end in zero. Most card numbers worldwide follow this rule.

A number is reported as valid only when the length looks correct and the Luhn checksum passes. The tool also detects the brand from the first digits, such as Visa, Mastercard, American Express, Discover and JCB.

credit-card-validator.h: Can it detect an active card?
credit-card-validator.p: No. The Luhn algorithm only proves the number is structurally valid. It cannot tell whether the card is active, has money, or belongs to a real person. Never enter a real card you do not own.

list: Checking whether a card number was typed correctly in forms and sign-ups.
Generating and verifying test card numbers while building payment UI.
Confirming that numbers on old receipts are well-formed.

credit-card-validator.p: No. Validation happens instantly in your browser with simple arithmetic. The number is never sent anywhere, so it is safe to test even payment cards you own.

roman-numeral-converter.p: Roman numerals use letters to represent values: I is 1, V is 5, X is 10, L is 50, C is 100, D is 500 and M is 1000. Values are usually written largest to smallest and added together.

roman-numeral-converter.h: When is a smaller numeral subtracted?
roman-numeral-converter.p: When a smaller numeral appears before a larger one, it is subtracted. IV means 4 (5 - 1), IX means 9 and CM means 900. This keeps the notation compact instead of writing four equal symbols.
This tool converts numbers from 1 to 3999. Larger values were written with special bars in antiquity, so the classic system shown here normally stops at MMMCMXCIX.

roman-numeral-converter.h: Where are Roman numerals used today?
list: Chapter and volume numbers in books and documents.
Years on buildings, clock faces and movie credits.
Rulers, popes and kings like Henry VIII or Louis XIV.
Outline numbering in essays and official papers.

roman-numeral-converter.h: How do I use the converter?
roman-numeral-converter.p: Type any whole number from 1 to 3999 and the Roman form appears instantly. Type a Roman numeral and the number is translated back. Both fields update live in both directions.

temperature-converter.p: Celsius and Fahrenheit are the most common scales, while Kelvin is the scientific absolute scale starting from absolute zero. The converter uses the standard formulas, so all three rows always agree.
To convert Celsius to Fahrenheit multiply by 9/5 and add 32. Fahrenheit to Celsius subtracts 32 and multiplies by 5/9. Kelvin is Celsius shifted by 273.15 degrees.

list: Celsius is the standard for weather and daily life in most countries.
Fahrenheit is common in the United States for weather and cooking.
Kelvin is used in science and engineering for absolute temperatures.

temperature-converter.p: Yes. Decimals like 21.5 are accepted, and the other two units are rounded to six digits for readability. Type into any of the three rows and the rest update instantly.
The formulas are exact, and the display rounds only for a cleaner result. Use the tool to convert recipes, weather forecasts, or lab values without doing the math by hand.

calculator.p: This calculator handles addition, subtraction, multiplication and division, plus percentage and square root. It works like a pocket calculator but runs right in your browser.

list: The % key divides the current value by 100.
The √ key computes the square root of the current value.
⌫ deletes the last digit and C clears everything.

calculator.p: Press an operator, enter the next number and press = for the result. Repeated operators are evaluated in order from left to right, like a classic simple calculator.

calculator.h: What happens when I divide by zero?
calculator.p: Divisions by zero show an error message instead of a result. Press C to start a fresh calculation.
The tool is designed for clicks and taps, so it also works comfortably on phones. Results are shown with up to twelve significant digits for accuracy.

html-to-text-converter.p:
It takes a block of HTML and returns clean plain text. Tags like
and

are removed while the visible text inside them is kept.

html-to-text-converter.h: Why remove script and style blocks?
html-to-text-converter.p: JavaScript and CSS are not part of the page content. Skipping them (the default) stops hidden code from leaking into your text and keeps the output clean.

list: Extracting article text from a copied web page.
Reading email HTML templates without markup.
Preparing HTML content for plain-text apps.

html-to-text-converter.h: Does it keep lists and paragraphs?
html-to-text-converter.p: Readable line breaks are preserved where the source structure has them, and long runs of blank lines are collapsed so the result stays tidy.
No. Conversion happens locally in your browser with the built-in HTML parser. Your content never leaves the device.

chmod-calculator.p: Unix files have three permission types — read (r), write (w) and execute (x) — for three groups: the owner, the group and everyone else. Each combination creates a three-digit mode.
Each set of rwx permissions is a value from 0 to 7. Read is worth 4, write 2 and execute 1. For example read and write gives 6, and all three gives 7.

list: chmod 755 — owner can read, write and execute; others can read and execute.
chmod 644 — owner can read and write; others can only read.
chmod 600 — only the owner can read and write.

chmod-calculator.p: Alongside the number, the symbolic notation like rwxr-xr-x describes the same permissions as ten characters: one for the type and nine for the three groups.

chmod-calculator.h: How do I use the calculator?
chmod-calculator.p: Tick the boxes for each permission and group, or press a preset button like 755 or 644. The numeric value updates live and can be copied in one click.

dice-roller.h: How many dice can I roll?
dice-roller.p: You can roll from 1 to 12 dice at once, and each die can have anywhere from 2 to 100 sides. The default is two six-sided dice.

dice-roller.h: Why support more than six sides?
dice-roller.p: Many tabletop games use dice like d8, d10, d12 and d20. This tool supports all of them and even unusual dice like a 100-sided d100.

dice-roller.h: What is shown after a roll?
dice-roller.p: The latest roll appears as large dice with each result, followed by the total. The last runs are listed in a history table so you can retell a lucky moment.
Results come from the browser's Math.random engine, which is random enough for games and tests. Each side of a die has an equal chance of appearing.

dice-roller.h: Can I use it for RPGs?
dice-roller.p: Yes. Set the number of dice and sides your character sheet needs, roll once and read the total. No setup, dice or download required.

coin-flipper.p: Each press of Flip produces heads or tails with a 50% chance for each, just like a real coin. The sides are picked instantly by the browser.
The tool counts how many times heads and tails have appeared and shows your longest run — the most consecutive flips landing on the same side.
The last throws are displayed as small chips so you can review a decision or double-check that a coin really came up fair over several flips.

coin-flipper.h: Where is a coin flip useful?
list: Settling a tie or deciding who goes first.
Choosing between two options without bias.
Teaching probability with real trial counts.

coin-flipper.p: Yes — each flip is independent and has an equal chance either way. Over many flips the counts should stay close to balanced.

word-frequency-counter.p: It splits your text into words, lowercases them and counts how often each one appears. The result is a table sorted from the most to the least repeated word.
Stop words are very common words like 'the', 'and' or 'of' that rarely carry meaning. Removing them (the default) makes the table focus on the meaningful vocabulary.

word-frequency-counter.h: How is it useful for writing?
word-frequency-counter.p: Authors use word frequency to check that key ideas are repeated consistently and to spot overused words that weaken the text.

word-frequency-counter.h: How useful is it for SEO?
word-frequency-counter.p: Keyword research is about how often terms appear. Paste page copy to see which terms dominate and confirm keywords are used naturally, not stuffed.
Words are sequences of letters and numbers. Turkish characters are supported and punctuation is ignored, so apostrophes and accented letters are handled correctly.

prime-factors-calculator.p: A prime factor is a factor that is a prime number. Factoring means breaking a number into its smallest possible building blocks, like 360 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 × 3 × 5.
Repeated factors are written with exponents to keep the result compact: 2 × 2 × 2 becomes 2^3. The display uses this notation so long numbers stay readable.

prime-factors-calculator.h: How large can the number be?
prime-factors-calculator.p: Numbers from 1 to 100,000,000 are supported. Larger values would require much heavier math in the browser, so the tool keeps a practical limit.

prime-factors-calculator.h: Can it decide if a number is prime?
prime-factors-calculator.p: Yes. A number with exactly one factor — itself, with exponent one — is reported as prime. Numbers below that are shown with their full factorization instead.
Factoring appears in school math, cryptography, and simplifying fractions. It is also a handy way to check whether a number divides into another cleanly.

angle-converter.p: Degrees are used in everyday life, radians in mathematics and programming, and gradians in surveying and some engineering. Converting between them is a constant need.
A full circle is 360 degrees, 2π radians or 400 gradians. So 180 degrees equals π radians and 100 gradians, the conversion used by this tool.
JavaScript and most math libraries expect angles in radians for functions like Math.sin and Math.cos. Typing the value here and copying the result avoids unit mistakes.
Yes. Values like 45.5 degrees are accepted, and the two other units update instantly with results rounded to eight decimal places.
The formulas are exact math; rounding is applied only for display. Converting 180 degrees always gives π radians, so no information is lost.

data-size-converter.h: What is the difference between 1000 and 1024?
data-size-converter.p: Decimal base uses 1 KB = 1000 bytes, which storage manufacturers use. Binary base uses 1 KiB = 1024 bytes, which operating systems often use. Choose the base that matches your situation.

list: Decimal (1000) for drive capacity and data plans.
Binary (1024) for RAM, memory and file sizes shown by many systems.

data-size-converter.h: Why see every unit at once?
data-size-converter.p: Seeing one size in all units at the same time makes comparisons easy, whether you are checking upload limits, disk usage or email attachment caps.

data-size-converter.h: Can I convert between bytes and TB?
data-size-converter.p: Yes. Every unit from byte to terabyte is listed in one table, and you can enter a value in any of them to see the rest.
Completely. The conversion is simple multiplication in your browser — nothing is calculated on a server or stored anywhere.

fibonacci-generator.p: The Fibonacci sequence starts with 0 and 1, and every following number is the sum of the two before it: 0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13 and so on.

fibonacci-generator.h: How many terms can I generate?
fibonacci-generator.p: Any number from 1 to 100 terms. The tool prints the list, the sum of all terms and the value of the last term so results are easy to check.
The sequence shows up in nature, art and trading. Spiral patterns of sunflowers and seashells follow the golden ratio derived from Fibonacci ratios.

fibonacci-generator.h: How is it useful in programming?
fibonacci-generator.p: Fibonacci is a classic exercise for learning loops, recursion and dynamic programming. Generating the sequence by hand is a quick way to test an implementation.
The numbers grow quickly — the 100th term is a 21-digit number. The tool keeps up to 100 terms, which is plenty for almost every practical use.

mortgage-calculator.h: What does this mortgage calculator show?
mortgage-calculator.p: It shows the monthly payment (principal and interest), the total amount paid over the full term and the total interest. A complete amortization table lists the principal, interest and remaining balance for every month.

mortgage-calculator.h: How is the monthly payment calculated?
mortgage-calculator.p: The standard amortization formula uses the loan amount, the monthly interest rate derived from your annual rate, and the number of months. The result keeps each month's payment level for the whole term.

mortgage-calculator.h: Does it include taxes and insurance?
mortgage-calculator.p: No. The payment covers principal and interest only. Property tax, home insurance and HOA fees vary by location, so the estimate is best used to compare terms and rates.

mortgage-calculator.h: Why does the down payment matter?
mortgage-calculator.p: A larger down payment reduces the loan amount, which lowers the monthly payment and the total interest you pay. It can also help you avoid private mortgage insurance.
The math follows the same amortization method lenders use. Your actual payment can differ slightly because of rate lock timing, fees and rounding, but the estimate is a reliable planning figure.

hours-calculator.p: It computes the time between a start and an end clock time. You get the duration in hours and minutes, the total number of minutes and the decimal hours often used for payroll.

hours-calculator.h: How do I use it for an overnight shift?
hours-calculator.p: Turn on the overnight option when work ends on the next day. The calculator then adds the extra 24 hours and returns the correct duration automatically.

hours-calculator.h: What is decimal hours and why use it?
hours-calculator.p: Decimal hours express time as a fraction of an hour, like 8.5 instead of 8 hours 30 minutes. Payroll systems and timesheets commonly expect this format.
No — the tool reports the time between the two clock times. To account for an unpaid break, simply adjust your end time by the break length.
Yes. The time pickers support a 24-hour day, so start and end can be anywhere between 00:00 and 23:59.

income-tax-calculator.p: It estimates the US federal income tax on your annual income using the 2025 marginal brackets. It shows taxable income, the tax owed, the effective rate and the marginal bracket your income falls into.
It is a fixed amount subtracted from gross income before tax. This tool applies the 2025 single-filer standard deduction of $14,600; uncheck the box to ignore it.

income-tax-calculator.h: Marginal vs. effective rate — what's the difference?
income-tax-calculator.p: The marginal rate is the tax rate on the last dollar earned. The effective rate is the average rate on the whole taxable income. They are usually different because a US tax bracket only applies to the income within that range.
State and local taxes, FICA/Social Security and Medicare, credits and itemized deductions are excluded. The estimate is useful for planning but not a substitute for tax software.
Each bracket's rate is applied only to the slice of income inside that bracket, then all slices are added together. The table below marks the bracket active for your income.

inflation-calculator.h: What does the inflation calculator do?
inflation-calculator.p: It converts a dollar amount from one year to its equivalent in another year using the Consumer Price Index (CPI). The result shows what the same money would buy at different times.
US CPI-U annual averages from 1970 to today. Because it relies on actual price history, results stay faithful to published inflation figures.

inflation-calculator.h: Why is my 2025 result different from the nominal number?
inflation-calculator.p: Inflation means prices rise over time, so an amount from the past buys less today, and a future amount needs more money to match past purchasing power. The tool only changes the value; it says nothing about interest earned.

inflation-calculator.h: Is there a limit on years?
inflation-calculator.p: The table starts at 1970. If you pick dates outside the range the result is not computed — this keeps every calculation reliable.
No. All calculations run locally in your browser and the CPI table is bundled with the page.

typing-speed-test.p: WPM (words per minute) is computed as correct characters typed divided by five (one average word) and then divided by the test duration in minutes. This matches the standard typing-test convention.
Accuracy is the percentage of characters you typed correctly. A high speed with low accuracy usually means you should slow down a little and focus on precision.

typing-speed-test.h: Can I choose the test length?
typing-speed-test.p: Yes — 15, 30 or 60 seconds. The 60-second test is the classic benchmark, while shorter tests are good for quick warm-ups.

typing-speed-test.h: What do the colors mean while typing?
typing-speed-test.p: Correct characters turn green. Wrong characters are highlighted red. The next letter to type is underlined so your eyes never lose the position.
Yes. A Turkish sample text is built in, and you can switch between English and Turkish with one tap without restarting the test.

css-units-converter.p: It converts between px, rem, em, %, vw and vh. The base units depend on the base font size (for rem and em), the viewport width (for vw) and the viewport height (for vh).

css-units-converter.h: What is the difference between rem and em?
css-units-converter.p: Both are relative to font size: rem uses the root font size, and em uses the font size of the current element. This tool assumes both follow the base font size you configure.

css-units-converter.h: Why do I need the viewport size?
css-units-converter.p: vw and vh are percentages of the viewport. Without knowing a concrete viewport, like 1920×1080, those units cannot be converted to a pixel value.

css-units-converter.h: How do I set custom base values?
css-units-converter.p: The default base font size is 16px and the default viewport is 1920×1080 — the most common desktop values. Change them to match your design system or target device.

css-units-converter.h: Is the percent unit interpreted correctly?
css-units-converter.p: Percentages are interpreted relative to the base font size, matching the common pattern for font sizes in CSS. The tool shows every unit side by side so results are easy to compare.

css-triangle-generator.h: How does a CSS triangle work?
css-triangle-generator.p: A triangle is created with borders on an element that has zero width and height. Each edge is a transparent border except one, and the visible border forms the triangle shape.
Eight directions: up, down, left, right and the four diagonals. Every option produces pure CSS — no images, SVG or extra elements needed.

css-triangle-generator.h: Can I change size and color?
css-triangle-generator.p: Yes. The size slider sets the base dimension in pixels and the color picker controls the triangle color. The generated code and the preview update in real time.

css-triangle-generator.h: How do I use the generated code?
css-triangle-generator.p: Copy the CSS block and paste it into your stylesheet. Apply the .triangle class to an empty element and the triangle appears exactly as previewed.

css-triangle-generator.h: Does it work on all browsers?
css-triangle-generator.p: Yes. Border techniques are supported by every modern browser and have been a standard trick in CSS for years — no fallbacks required.

countdown-timer.h: How do I start a countdown?
countdown-timer.p: Enter hours, minutes and seconds, then press Start. The big display counts down second by second, and the inputs are locked while the timer runs.
Yes. Press Pause to stop the countdown at its current position, then press Start again to resume from exactly where it left off.

countdown-timer.h: What happens when time runs out?
countdown-timer.p: The display freezes at 00:00:00 and a 'Time is up' message appears. Use the Restart button to run the same countdown again.

countdown-timer.h: Does it keep running in the background?
countdown-timer.p: The timer counts down while the tab is open. Very long background timing is not guaranteed, so keep the tab visible for exact tracking.

countdown-timer.h: Is a sound played at the end?
countdown-timer.p: No sound is played — the timer ends silently with a visual message, so it is safe to use in quiet rooms and offices.

image-grid-splitter.h: What is the image grid splitter used for?
image-grid-splitter.p: It cuts a photo into equal slices arranged in a grid. The most common use is the three-by-three Instagram profile grid, where nine matching tiles form one large image.

image-grid-splitter.h: How do I choose the grid size?
image-grid-splitter.p: Pick any combination of rows and columns from 1 to 6. A 3×3 grid gives nine square slices; a 2×3 grid gives six slices often used for stories and banners.

image-grid-splitter.h: Are the slices cropped or resized?
image-grid-splitter.p: Each slice is an exact cut of the original image keeping its proportions. The source is not stretched, so parts may be cropped only where the grid requires it.

image-grid-splitter.h: How do I download the pieces?
image-grid-splitter.p: Every slice is rendered as a PNG inside the preview grid. Tap the download link on any tile (or save the image) to store it on your device.

image-grid-splitter.h: Does the image leave my device?
image-grid-splitter.p: No. The image is opened and cut locally in your browser with the HTML canvas. Nothing is uploaded to a server.

ascii-art-generator.p: The image is downsized to a tight grid and every cell is turned into its brightness. A ramp of characters, from a space up to the @ sign, replaces each brightness so a picture emerges from text.

ascii-art-generator.h: Why does the output have a fixed width?
ascii-art-generator.p: The width slider controls the character columns of the result. A realistic desktop value is 100–160 columns; very small sizes lose detail and very large ones overflow the screen.

ascii-art-generator.h: What does the invert option do?
ascii-art-generator.p: Inverting swaps the character ramp, so dark areas become bright and bright areas become dark. It helps when an image has poor contrast.

ascii-art-generator.h: Can I copy the art somewhere?
ascii-art-generator.p: The generated text is rendered in a plain pre-block. Select it and copy as keyboard text, then paste it anywhere that accepts plain text.
Any common image format your browser can open works. The source is scaled internally, so large photos are handled just as easily as small icons.

pixelate-image.p: The image is first scaled down to a tiny canvas — one block per pixel cell — then scaled back up without smoothing. The result is the classic chunky pixel look.

pixelate-image.h: How do I control the effect?
pixelate-image.p: Drag the pixel size slider. Small values like 4–8 give a subtle blocky texture, while values of 32–64 produce the heavy retro game look.
The output is downloaded as a PNG file, so the pixelated preview keeps full quality no matter how many times it is opened.

pixelate-image.h: Does it work with all image types?
pixelate-image.p: Yes. Any format your browser can display — JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF and more — can be pixelated. Large images are handled in memory.
No. The original file stays untouched on your device. The tool only creates a new pixelated version you can preview and download.

vigenere-cipher.p: It is a classical polyalphabetic cipher where a keyword shifts each letter by a different amount. The same keyword encrypts and decrypts, so it is called a symmetric cipher.

vigenere-cipher.h: How do I encrypt a message?
vigenere-cipher.p: Type the plain text, enter a keyword and keep Encrypt selected. Each letter is shifted by the corresponding keyword letter, repeating the keyword until the message ends.
Select Decrypt and enter the same keyword that was used to encrypt. The process is reversed and the original text is restored.
Yes. The alphabet includes Turkish letters like Ç, Ğ, İ, Ö, Ş and Ü, so Turkish text encrypts and decrypts correctly. Other characters are kept unchanged.

vigenere-cipher.h: Is this secure for real secrets?
vigenere-cipher.p: No. The Vigenère cipher is easy to break with modern computers and is used for learning and fun rather than protection. Do not rely on it for sensitive data.

punctuation-remover.p: It strips every punctuation mark — like .,!?;:'"()[] — from the text and keeps letters, numbers, spaces and line breaks.
Yes. Tick 'Keep apostrophes' to preserve possessive and contraction apostrophes such as in isn't or John's.
Tick 'Keep hyphens' so compound words like well-known or 24-hour stay intact instead of merging into one word.

punctuation-remover.h: How do I know how much was removed?
punctuation-remover.p: The tool reports the exact number of punctuation characters that were removed from your text, so you can compare input and output.
It is handy for cleaning text for machine learning, preparing data for scripts, or producing a simplified plain-text version of a document.

anagram-solver.p: An anagram is a rearrangement of letters that forms another word or phrase. This tool lists every unique arrangement of the letters you enter, whether or not it is a real word.
No. The solver generates all letter combinations and lets you scan them yourself. That keeps it fast, offline and unlimited.

anagram-solver.h: How many letters can I enter?
anagram-solver.p: Up to nine letters. Beyond that the number of permutations grows explosively, so the tool caps the input at nine to stay responsive.
Yes. Duplicate letters produce only unique results, so a word like 'toot' does not generate identical anagrams over and over.

anagram-solver.h: What are the results sorted by?
anagram-solver.p: Alphabetically. When the result set is very large, the first 2,000 are shown and a marker tells you more exist.

keyword-combiner.h: How does the keyword combiner work?
keyword-combiner.p: Every line in the first box is paired with every line in the second box. If list A has 5 entries and list B has 4, you get 20 combined keywords.
Long-tail keywords with real search intent are built from these combinations. They fill content calendars, PPC campaigns and meta tags with fresh ideas.
Result keys remove duplicate lines, so the same pair never appears twice even if it exists in your source lists.

keyword-combiner.h: How do I copy the results?
keyword-combiner.p: Press the Copy button or select the output area with your mouse. Each combination sits on its own line, ready for pasting into spreadsheets and tools.
No. Combining happens locally in your browser; nothing is uploaded.

title-length-checker.p: It compares your title against ~60 characters and ~580 pixels and your meta description against ~160 characters and ~920 pixels — the typical limits Google uses in search results.

title-length-checker.h: Why check pixels instead of characters?
title-length-checker.p: Google truncates titles and descriptions by pixel width rather than character count. Caps, wide letters and punctuation affect width, so char-only tools can lie about truncation.
Each bar fills up to the pixel limit. When it stays in green the snippet is safe; when it turns red the snippet likely gets truncated with ellipsis (…).
It is an estimate based on common glyph widths for the default search font. Actual rendering varies slightly by font and language, so treat it as a reliable but approximate guide.
A well-formed, under-limit title and description are fully displayed, which usually improves click-through from search results — one of the foundations of better SEO.

magic-8-ball.h: How does the magic 8 ball work?
magic-8-ball.p: Think of a yes-or-no question, press Shake and the ball picks one of the classic 20 answers at random. It is a toy, so treat the outcome as playful rather than serious.
The full classic set is included — positive answers like 'It is certain', negative ones like 'Cannot predict now' and vague ones like 'Ask again later'.
The answer is chosen with a random pick on every shake, and a small counter shows how many questions have been asked in this session.

magic-8-ball.h: Can I use it on my phone?
magic-8-ball.p: Yes — the ball and shake button scale to the smallest screens, so it works well as a quick break on mobile.
It solves trivial decisions fast and brings a little fun to everyday questions. The design mirrors the classic toy, so it feels instantly familiar.

fuel-cost-calculator.p: Fuel cost = distance ÷ 100 × average consumption × fuel price. Example: 300 km with 7 L/100 km and a fuel price of 45 results in (300 ÷ 100) × 7 × 45 = 945.

fuel-cost-calculator.h: Which fuel price should I use?
fuel-cost-calculator.p: Use the average price per liter from your region or station. For long trips, enter the round-trip distance so the result covers the whole route.

plagiarism-checker.h: How does the similarity score work?
plagiarism-checker.p: The tool compares two texts using the Dice coefficient on character bigrams. Texts that share many identical two-character sequences score higher, which is a strong sign of copied content.
No. The comparison runs fully in your browser, so the text you paste never leaves your device.

number-to-words.h: How large a number can I convert?
number-to-words.p: The converter supports whole numbers up to 999 trillion, which covers practically every invoice and check amount.

number-to-words.h: Does it handle cents and decimals?
number-to-words.p: The tool accepts whole numbers. For amounts with decimals, convert the integer part first and add the fraction manually.

image-rotator.h: Is the image uploaded to a server?
image-rotator.p: No. The image is loaded and edited with the HTML Canvas API in your browser, and the download is generated locally. Nothing is uploaded.

image-rotator.h: In which format can I download?
image-rotator.p: The rotated or flipped result is exported as PNG. For photos, PNG keeps full quality.

xml-sitemap-generator.h: Where do I put the generated sitemap?
xml-sitemap-generator.p: Save the output as sitemap.xml in the root of your site (for example https://www.freetoolsy.com/sitemap.xml), then submit the URL via Google Search Console.

xml-sitemap-generator.h: How many URLs can a sitemap list?
xml-sitemap-generator.p: A single sitemap can contain up to 50,000 URLs and stay under 50 MB. If you have more, split it into several sitemap files.

email-validator.p: It checks the format (name@domain.tld), that the top-level domain is a real and common one, and whether the local part looks role-based such as info@ or admin@.

email-validator.h: Can it prove an email exists?
email-validator.p: No. A server-side check would be needed to confirm a mailbox exists, and this tool stays fully private and local.

word-scrambler.p: A word scrambler takes every word in your text and rearranges its letters. Keep the first and last letters fixed and the output still looks like real words, or fully randomize everything for puzzles and brain teasers. The result is ready to copy and paste anywhere.
Create anagram challenges for friends, practice reading in a new language, or briefly anonymize names inside short texts. It is also a quick way to produce playful usernames and captions.

hashtag-generator.p: Social media posts perform better when hashtags are consistent: no spaces, no punctuation and clearly grouped by topic. This tool turns a normal phrase into ready-to-use hashtags so a broken tag never ends up in your post.

The minimum length option removes tiny, low-value tags, while the common words option skips generic words every post already contains. Keeping only strong, specific hashtags boosts visibility without spam.

acronym-generator.p: An acronym generator reads a phrase word by word and keeps the first letter of each word. The result is a compact uppercase abbreviation. The dots option adds a period after every letter, which fits many official and company name styles.

Naming a company, a product line or a course, shortening long official titles, or building study abbreviations like formula and chapter names. It also helps turn multi-word search terms into memorable codes.

palindrome-checker.p: A palindrome is a word, phrase or number that reads exactly the same forwards and backwards. The checker compares the text with its reverse and tells you instantly whether it matches.

palindrome-checker.h: How does the ignore option work?
palindrome-checker.p: Turning on the ignore option removes spaces, punctuation and letter case before comparing. This follows the spirit of real palindromes, where the readable letters matter more than the exact characters.

http-status-codes.h: How do HTTP status codes work?
http-status-codes.p: Every web request ends with a three-digit status code from the server. The first digit shows the class: 1xx informational, 2xx success, 3xx redirect, 4xx client error and 5xx server error. Knowing the code tells you exactly what went wrong.

http-status-codes.h: Which codes matter most day to day?
http-status-codes.p: 404 means a page was not found, 403 means access is denied and 301 is a permanent redirect. On the server side, 500 is a general internal error while 503 usually means the service is temporarily unavailable.

csv-formatter.p: Raw CSV viewed in a text editor is hard to scan: fields run together and quoted columns hide the true structure. Formatting splits each record into visible cells so you can spot misaligned columns, missing values or wrong delimiters in seconds.

The parser reads every line and respects double quotes, so fields that contain the delimiter or line breaks stay intact. Switch the delimiter for data that uses semicolons or tabs, and copy the result as TSV to paste it into any spreadsheet.

days-until-calculator.h: How is the day count calculated?
days-until-calculator.p: The calculator works with real calendar dates, so month lengths, leap years and year boundaries are all handled correctly. Pick a start date and a target date; the result shows total days plus weeks and remaining days.
When the target date falls before the start date, the result is shown with a past marker. This is handy for checking how long ago an event happened or for verifying record-keeping windows.

running-pace-converter.h: How does pace relate to speed?
running-pace-converter.p: Pace is the time needed to run one kilometer, and speed is the distance covered in one hour. The converter divides 3600 seconds by your pace to give the average speed, so 5:00 per kilometer equals exactly 12 km/h.

The tool projects finish times for 5K, 10K, half marathon and full marathon by multiplying your pace by the official distance. These are linear estimates and do not account for hills, weather or fatigue during the race.

savings-goal-calculator.p: The remaining amount is your goal minus what you already have. Dividing that by your monthly saving gives the number of months needed, and dividing it by a target number of months gives the monthly amount you should save.

savings-goal-calculator.h: How can I reach the goal faster?
savings-goal-calculator.p: Small increases in monthly saving shorten the timeline far more than they cost. Breaking a large goal into milestones also keeps motivation high, and automating the transfer makes the plan consistent.

rock-paper-scissors.p: Pick rock, paper or scissors and the computer picks one at random. Rock crushes scissors, scissors cut paper and paper covers rock. Identical choices are a tie. Every round updates your three scores.
Each round the computer selects randomly from the three options with equal probability, so there is no pattern to learn and no advantage for either side. The result is determined purely by chance.

horoscope.p: The tropical zodiac divides the year into twelve periods, each linked to a constellation. Enter any date and the tool matches it to the correct period, then shows the sign name, element, date range and a short personality summary.

horoscope.h: Is it meant to be taken seriously?
horoscope.p: No. Sign descriptions are broad and written for entertainment. Real astrology and astronomy are very different fields; this tool is a fun reference for names, birthdays and party games.

text-escape-unescape.p: In JSON and JavaScript, certain characters have special meaning: quotes open and close strings, and backslashes start escape sequences. Escaping prefixes those characters with a backslash so a string can be stored or embedded safely.
API logs, config dumps and database exports often arrive fully escaped and hard to read. Pasting such text here decodes it back to plain, readable content in one click instead of editing it by hand.

emoji-remover.h: What does an emoji remover do?
emoji-remover.p: It scans your text and deletes every emoji, pictograph, decorative symbol and the invisible variation selectors attached to them. What remains is clean plain text that is safe to paste anywhere, including into strict editors, databases and scripts.

emoji-remover.h: When should I clean emojis from my text?
emoji-remover.p: Use it before publishing copy where emojis are not allowed, when exporting data into systems that reject Unicode pictographs, or simply when you want a neat, symbol-free version of a message to reuse.

reading-time-calculator.p: The tool counts the words in your text and divides by the reading speed you choose, which defaults to 200 words per minute. The result is rounded up to whole minutes so headings are never cut short.

A 60 words-per-minute user reads three times slower than a 180 words-per-minute one. Set a realistic speed for your own audience and you will get a far better estimate for blog intros, video scripts or meeting handouts.

totp-generator.h: Where does the code come from?
totp-generator.p: Your Base32 secret is decoded and combined with the current Unix time divided into 30-second steps. A one-way HMAC-SHA1 signature produces a 6-digit code that matches exactly what your authenticator app shows.
The whole calculation uses the Web Crypto API inside your browser page. The secret never leaves your device, which makes this a trustworthy way to test your own 2FA keys on this site.

url-parser.h: What parts of a URL are shown?
url-parser.p: You get protocol, host, hostname, port, path, query string, hash, username, password and origin. Every part is split exactly the way modern browsers parse it, so the results match what your code actually receives.

Debugging redirects, validating links in configuration files, reading authorization tokens inside query strings or simply learning how URLs are put together. The normalized URL copy button is handy for sharing a clean version of a messy link.

js-minifier.p: It trims the indentation at the start of every line, deletes blank lines and removes lines that are only comments. Because it never touches the inside of strings or template literals, the meaning of your code is preserved exactly.

js-minifier.h: Is this the same as a full minifier?
js-minifier.p: No. A full minifier rewrites variables and strips every unnecessary byte. This tool is the safe, readable middle ground: it shrinks code noticeably for casual use without ever risking a syntax break.

mime-type-finder.p: A standardized label such as image/png or application/json that tells servers and browsers what kind of content a file contains. Using the right one matters for downloads, uploads, email attachments and API responses.

mime-type-finder.h: When would I need this tool?
mime-type-finder.p: When configuring a web server's content types, validating file uploads, preparing OpenGraph or link previews, or double-checking an extension you cannot remember. Searching by type is handy for finding every extension a format class uses.

percentage-change-calculator.p: The change equals (new value - old value) divided by the absolute value of the old value, then multiplied by 100. Dividing by the absolute value means a drop from 100 to 50 is exactly the reverse of a rise from 50 to 100.

percentage-change-calculator.h: What about a zero starting point?
percentage-change-calculator.p: Percentages need a reference point, and division by zero is not defined. When the old value is zero the tool shows the absolute difference instead and clearly warns that a percentage cannot be computed.

fuel-economy-calculator.p: L/100 km is how many litres a car uses per hundred kilometres, the European standard. MPG is miles per US gallon, common in North America. km/L is the simplest: the distance one litre covers.

Car specs and reviews use different units depending on their region. Converting helps you compare fuel costs across markets and understand figures from foreign tests or manufacturers. The conversion factor is baked in, so results are instant and correct.

electricity-cost-calculator.p: Watts are converted to kilowatts first, then multiplied by the hours used per day and the days used per month. Yearly figures are simply the monthly ones multiplied by 12. This is the same formula most energy meters use.

electricity-cost-calculator.h: How do I read the cost results?
electricity-cost-calculator.p: Multiply your monthly kilowatt-hours by the price you pay per kWh. The tool does this for you and shows both monthly and yearly costs, making it easy to compare appliances like fridges, TVs or heaters.

calories-burned-calculator.h: How does the MET formula work?
calories-burned-calculator.p: Each activity has a MET value measuring how many times more energy it burns than resting. Calories equal MET multiplied by 3.5, your weight in kilograms and duration in minutes, divided by 200.

MET values are averages taken from large population studies, so results are a solid guide for planning, not a medical measurement. Speed, fitness and terrain all shift the real number, usually by ten to twenty percent.

image-combiner.p: Both images are decoded and drawn next to each other onto one canvas whose width is the sum of both widths and whose height matches the taller image. The space left below the shorter image stays white.
Before-and-after comparisons, simple collages, stitching two halves of a screenshot or pairing a photo with a diagram. The resulting PNG has the exact combined dimensions and is ready to download.

image-flipper.h: What is the difference between flip and rotate?
image-flipper.p: Rotating turns the image around its center. Flipping mirrors it, so text becomes unreadable and the orientation changes relative to a real mirror. Both are useful in design, but they produce very different results.

image-flipper.h: When would I flip an image?
image-flipper.p: Fixing mirror images from front cameras, preparing thumbnails, duplicating elements for symmetry in mockups, or just changing the look of an asset. The flip controls are instant and the output downloads as a clean PNG.

sitemap-url-extractor.p: It parses the XML of your sitemap and collects the content of every loc tag, which is where search engines look for page URLs. Comments and surrounding markup are ignored, so the output is a clean list of links.

sitemap-url-extractor.h: Why extract URLs from a sitemap?
sitemap-url-extractor.p: To verify how many pages a site exposes to search engines, to build a full URL inventory for migration or audits, or to check that indexed pages still return valid responses. Copying the whole list takes one click.

joke-generator.h: Where do the jokes come from?
joke-generator.p: The page ships with a small hand-picked selection of programming jokes in both English and Turkish. The generator picks one at random, and the button highlights a new one every time.

joke-generator.h: Can I keep going after the first laugh?
joke-generator.p: Certainly. Press the button as many times as you like. The current joke is skipped on the next press, so you keep getting fresh material instead of the same one twice in a row.

random-quote-generator.p: Quotes are stored in a curated list that ships with the page. Every press picks a random entry and deliberately avoids the previous one, which keeps the generator feeling fresh.
Completely in your browser. There is no server request, no tracking and no account, which makes it perfect for a quick dose of inspiration in the middle of a busy day.
