guess-the-number.h: How do I win as fast as possible?
guess-the-number.p: Always guess the middle of the remaining range. Start at 50, then cut the range in half with every hint. This binary search strategy wins every game in seven guesses at most.
The page counts the attempts you used and offers a play again button that picks a brand new secret number. Try to beat your previous score with the same strategy.

time-zone-converter.h: What is a Time Zone Converter?
time-zone-converter.p: A Time Zone Converter takes a specific date and time in one zone and shows the matching date and time in another. Because a time zone is only an offset from UTC and that offset changes with daylight saving, the same moment can be 30 September in Tokyo and 29 September in Los Angeles.

time-zone-converter.h: How time zones and offsets work
time-zone-converter.p: The world is divided into roughly 400 zones, each described by a UTC offset such as UTC+3 or UTC-5 and, in most cases, an IANA name like Europe/Istanbul or America/New_York. The offset alone is not enough: names follow the legal changes of each region, so a converter that uses real zone data is correct through every daylight saving transition.

time-zone-converter.h: When a time difference is not a fixed number
time-zone-converter.p: Most comparisons fail because the offset was assumed constant. Between March and November London sits seven hours ahead of New York, but during the short period when one side has already switched and the other has not, the gap becomes eight or six hours. This is exactly why scheduling tools convert the date, not just the clock time.

The most common job is booking: reading a meeting invitation written in another zone, planning a release window, or working out when a support team on the other side of the Atlantic starts. Remote teams also convert working hours, and travellers use it to check when a flight lands and what time dinner is at the destination.
Yes. The conversion happens in your browser using the built-in time zone database, so no date you check is sent or stored. No signup, completely free.

Writers can check length limits before publishing, students can review essays, and editors can clean lists or standardize copied text. Developers and content teams can also extract useful details, convert entities, or reverse text for specific workflows. Each tool is focused on a small task, so you can paste or enter text, choose the relevant action, and copy the result. Most processing happens directly in your browser, making these utilities convenient for quick everyday edits on desktop or mobile.

faq.question: What are free online text tools?
faq.answer: They are browser-based utilities for counting, cleaning, converting, comparing, and generating text. Choose a tool for one task, enter or paste your text, then review and copy the result.

faq.question: Do I need to create an account?
faq.answer: No account is required to use these text tools. Open a tool page and start working without signing up or installing an app.

faq.question: Are these tools safe to use?
faq.answer: Text processing for these utilities runs in your browser, so the text you enter is not uploaded by the tool for processing. Avoid entering sensitive information on any shared or untrusted device.

security.description: Online security tools provide practical helpers for creating, checking, and working with security-related values. This category includes password generation and strength checks, cryptographic hashes, encryption utilities, file checksums, and other focused safeguards. They can help individuals create stronger credentials, developers verify test data, and administrators inspect a digest or file fingerprint during routine work. The tools are designed for quick browser-based tasks and explain the kind of output they produce, but they do not replace a complete security review, a password manager, or professional cryptographic guidance. Use them to learn, prepare, or validate non-sensitive material, and always protect private keys, production secrets, and confidential data according to your organization’s security practices.

Generate a hash for a test string or compare a downloaded file checksum with a trusted reference.
Encrypt or decrypt sample text while learning how a particular cryptographic workflow behaves.
Prepare non-production test values for development, documentation, or troubleshooting.

faq.question: What can I do with online security tools?
faq.answer: They can help generate passwords, estimate password strength, create hashes, check file integrity, or perform supported encryption tasks. Use each tool only for the specific operation it describes.

faq.question: Should I enter production passwords or private keys?
faq.answer: Do not enter secrets into a tool unless you have reviewed its behavior and your organization permits it. Prefer local, approved security software for production credentials and sensitive keys.

faq.question: Do these tools replace professional security software?
faq.answer: No. They are convenient helpers for individual tasks, not a replacement for vetted security products, secure key management, or a broader security assessment.

Software developers can inspect payloads, format configuration files, prepare test values, and check conversions without switching between several desktop apps. Students and technical writers can use the same tools to understand formats and create examples. Most utilities are designed for immediate input and output, with clear results that are easy to copy. Review generated code and decoded data before using them in production, especially when handling credentials or confidential project information.

Encode a URL parameter, inspect a JWT’s readable parts, or convert Base64 data while troubleshooting integration behavior.
Generate UUIDs, test a regular expression, or convert color and CSS units while building an interface.
Check subnet details or prepare sample values for a bug report, lesson, or technical document.

faq.question: Which developer tasks can these tools help with?
faq.answer: They support common formatting, validation, encoding, conversion, testing, and generation tasks across code, text, and web data. Open the tool that matches your input format or development task.

faq.question: Can I use the generated output in production?
faq.answer: Review and test output in your project before deployment. These tools assist with individual tasks but do not replace code review, application tests, or security checks.

faq.question: Is my code or data uploaded?
faq.answer: Most tools in this collection process input in your browser. Do not paste credentials, private tokens, or confidential source code into a page unless your security requirements allow it.

calculation.description: Calculation tools help turn everyday numbers, dates, measurements, and rates into clear results. This category includes percentage, VAT, BMI, age, date-difference, discount, tip, loan, unit, and other practical calculators. Shoppers can estimate a sale price, freelancers can calculate tax-inclusive totals, and households can split a bill or compare measurements. Students and professionals can use focused calculators to check arithmetic or understand how a value changes when an input changes. Enter the values requested by a tool and review the result before making a decision. These calculators are intended for convenience and general information; financial, tax, health, and legal decisions may require current local rules or advice from a qualified professional.
useCases: Work out a percentage increase, discount amount, or final price while comparing products or planning a budget.
Estimate VAT, a tip, or each person’s share when preparing an invoice or splitting a restaurant bill.
Convert measurements, compare two dates, or calculate an age for travel, school, or project planning.
Explore a loan payment or BMI estimate as an initial reference, then confirm important decisions with an expert.

faq.question: Are these calculators suitable for financial or health decisions?
faq.answer: They provide calculations based on the values entered, but are not professional financial, tax, medical, or legal advice. Confirm important decisions with a qualified professional and current local guidance.

faq.question: What information do I need to use a calculator?
faq.answer: It depends on the task. Each calculator labels the inputs it needs, such as an amount and rate, two dates, a height and weight, or a measurement and unit.

faq.question: Can I use the calculators on my phone?
faq.answer: Yes. The calculators run in a web browser and can be opened on a phone, tablet, or computer without installing a separate app.

image.description: Image tools help you prepare visual files for websites, social posts, documents, and design projects. This category includes utilities for compressing, resizing, converting, cropping, rotating, splitting, and inspecting images, along with color-related helpers. Creators can reduce file dimensions before publishing, designers can create consistent assets, and small businesses can make images fit a product listing or newsletter. Many tools provide a preview so you can check the result before downloading it. Image formats and quality settings affect appearance and file size, so inspect the exported file in its intended context. These browser-based helpers are useful for quick edits, but they are not a replacement for full-featured image-editing software when a project needs advanced retouching or layered composition.
useCases: Resize or crop a photo to fit a website banner, profile image, product listing, or social media layout.
Compress a large image before adding it to a page or sending it by email, then review visual quality.
Convert an image to a format accepted by a content system, design tool, or document workflow.
Pick colors from an image or split artwork into evenly sized tiles for a planned layout.

faq.question: Which image tasks can these tools handle?
faq.answer: Depending on the selected tool, you can resize, compress, crop, rotate, convert, split, or inspect image files. Check each tool’s supported formats and options before processing.

faq.question: Will compression reduce image quality?
faq.answer: Some compression settings can change visual quality. Preview the result and compare it with the original before using or sharing the exported file.

faq.question: Do I need to install image-editing software?
faq.answer: No installation is needed for these quick browser-based tasks. For advanced retouching, layered work, or professional color management, dedicated editing software may be more suitable.

seo.description: SEO tools help site owners and content teams inspect how pages may appear in search and improve common on-page details. This category includes slug and meta tag generators, SERP previews, keyword density checks, readability analysis, and other practical helpers. Bloggers can draft clearer snippets, marketers can review keyword usage, and developers can prepare page metadata before publishing. Use the results as a starting point: search engines may rewrite titles and descriptions, ranking systems change, and no single score guarantees better positions. Pair these tools with useful original content, accessible pages, fast performance, and data from search analytics. The tools are intended to make routine checks easier, not to promise rankings or replace a complete technical and editorial SEO review.
useCases: Draft a concise page title and meta description before publishing a new article or landing page.
Preview how a page snippet may appear and revise copy that is unclear or poorly focused.
Review keyword frequency and readability while editing a guide for a specific audience.
Create a clean URL slug or inspect page metadata during a content audit.

faq.question: Can an SEO tool guarantee higher rankings?
faq.answer: No. These tools help check and prepare page elements, but rankings depend on many factors such as relevance, quality, competition, technical accessibility, and search engine systems.

faq.question: Are SERP previews exactly what Google will display?
faq.answer: They are visual estimates. Search engines can choose different snippets or rewrite titles and descriptions based on the query and page content.

faq.question: How should I use keyword and readability scores?
faq.answer: Treat them as editing signals, not targets to maximize. Write useful, natural content for readers, then use analytics and search performance data to guide improvements.

fun.description: Fun tools offer lightweight ways to make a choice, run a quick activity, or add a playful moment to a group or solo task. This category includes random name and number pickers, dice and coin tools, timers, and other simple interactive utilities. Teachers can use them to choose a classroom participant, friends can settle a low-stakes decision, and teams can add a short break to a meeting. Many activities work with a few clicks and show the result immediately, without requiring a separate app. They are designed for entertainment and everyday convenience rather than regulated drawings, gambling, or high-stakes selection. For formal contests, use a process with documented rules and independently verifiable randomness.
useCases: Pick a volunteer or discussion order during a classroom activity or team meeting.
Roll virtual dice or flip a coin when playing a casual game or making a low-stakes choice.
Set a countdown or stopwatch for a study session, presentation practice, or quick challenge.
Draw a random number for a classroom exercise, informal raffle, or game prompt.

faq.question: What are fun online tools used for?
faq.answer: They support casual activities such as random picks, dice rolls, coin flips, and timing short tasks. Choose a tool based on the activity you want to run.

faq.question: Can I use a random picker for an official prize draw?
faq.answer: These tools are intended for casual use and do not provide an audited drawing process. For official promotions, follow applicable rules and use a documented, independently verifiable method.

faq.answer: No. Open a tool in your web browser and use its controls directly. No separate app or account is needed.

sections.p: The web is full of similar tools, but most require signup, collect data or clutter the interface with ads. Our priority is plain tools that take no time to learn and no extra setup. Each tool is designed to do one thing well: count text, generate passwords, format JSON.

privacy.desc: FreetoolsY privacy policy: which data is collected, cookies, third-party ads and your rights.

sections.p: FreetoolsY ("we", "the site") offers free online tools at https://www.freetoolsy.com. This policy explains what information is collected while you use the site and how it is used. By using the site you accept this policy.

Most of our tools run in your browser; the text, numbers or data you enter are not sent to or stored on our servers. The site may process certain technical data (IP address, browser type, visited pages, device information) for standard web analytics and advertising services.

The site uses cookies to remember preferences (such as theme choice) and to measure service quality. Analytics and advertising scripts are only loaded after you accept them through the cookie banner; your choice is stored in your browser's localStorage under the key "cookie_consent" and you can change it at any time by clearing your browser data. You can allow or block cookies from your browser settings at any time; blocking them does not stop most tools from working.
This site may use third-party ad providers such as Google AdSense for revenue. Google may use cookies (including DART cookies) to personalize ad delivery. See the
sections.post: for details on Google's data usage. Users can opt out of personalized ads in

sections.p: The site uses Google Analytics and GoatCounter to understand visitor statistics. Google Analytics uses cookies to analyze site usage. GoatCounter is a privacy-focused, open source analytics service: it does not use cookies, does not store personal data and does not build cross-site profiles. Neither service is loaded until you give consent through the cookie banner, and the information collected is processed anonymously.
The site takes reasonable measures to protect personal data. However, no method of transmission over the internet is 100% secure, so absolute security cannot be guaranteed.
Under KVKK and GDPR you have the right to access, correct, delete or object to the processing of your data. You can reach us through the contact section for any request.
This policy may be updated from time to time due to legal requirements or service changes. Updates are published on this page, with notice on the site for significant changes.

Play with your cat in the evening. The cat runs and jumps. A happy cat purrs. The house is heated in winter. Take care of your cat at home.
readabilityScore.complexSampleText: Notwithstanding the epistemological limitations inherent in contemporary qualitative methodologies, the comprehensive investigation of longitudinal socioeconomic disparities necessitates a comprehensive reconsideration of institutional accountability frameworks. Phenomenological investigations concerning the characterization of multidimensional systemic vulnerabilities demonstrate that institutionalized discrimination perpetuates structurally inequitable outcomes across heterogeneous demographic cohorts, thereby fundamentally destabilizing conventional epistemological paradigms. Furthermore, notwithstanding the predominant institutionalization of deliberative democratic mechanisms, contemporary macroeconomic fluctuations have consequentially destabilized comprehensive socioeconomic stabilization strategies that policymakers have historically considered foundational to equitable distributive justice methodologies.

httpStatusCodes.tip: Codes in the 4xx range mean a client mistake, while 5xx codes mean the server failed to fulfill the request.

csvFormatter.empty: Paste CSV data to preview it as a table.
csvFormatter.tip: Quoted fields containing the delimiter are handled correctly. Copying as TSV makes pasting into spreadsheets just work.

daysUntilCalculator.future: The target date is in the future.
daysUntilCalculator.pastNote: The target date is in the past.
daysUntilCalculator.empty: Pick both dates to count the days.
daysUntilCalculator.tip: The difference uses calendar days, so leap days and month lengths are taken into account.

runningPaceConverter.empty: Enter a pace to calculate speed and race times.
runningPaceConverter.tip: A pace of 5:00 per kilometer equals exactly 12 km/h. The marathon distance includes the official race distance of 42.195 km.

savingsGoalCalculator.tip: The calculator ignores interest. For long goals, even a small monthly amount adds up quickly and consistency matters most.

rockPaperScissors.tip: Rock beats scissors, scissors beat paper, and paper beats rock. The computer picks randomly every round.

horoscope.empty: Pick a date to find the sign.
horoscope.tip: This is a fun reference only: signs follow the tropical zodiac and are not meant as fortune telling.

textEscapeUnescape.invalid: The input cannot be unescaped. Check for missing backslashes.
textEscapeUnescape.empty: Type some text and choose escape or unescape.
textEscapeUnescape.tip: Escaping converts quotes and backslashes so a string is valid inside JSON and JavaScript source code.

emojiRemover.empty: Paste some text above to clean out the emojis.
emojiRemover.tip: The tool removes emojis and common decorative symbols. All processing happens locally in your browser.

readingTimeCalculator.empty: Paste some text above to estimate its reading time.
readingTimeCalculator.tip: Counts words in your browser and divides by the speed you choose. Default is 200 words per minute.

totpGenerator.empty: Enter at least 10 characters from your 2FA secret key.
totpGenerator.tip: Computes a TOTP (RFC 6238) code locally with the Web Crypto API. Only use keys you trust on this page, although nothing leaves your browser.

urlParser.invalid: That does not look like a valid URL.
urlParser.empty: Paste a full URL above to break it into its parts.
urlParser.tip: Parsing follows the WHATWG URL standard and runs locally in your browser.

jsMinifier.empty: Paste JavaScript code above to clean it up.
jsMinifier.tip: Removes blank lines, leading indentation and whole-line comments. String literals and template strings are left untouched.

mimeTypeFinder.notFound: No MIME type found for this extension.
mimeTypeFinder.tip: Finds the MIME type for common file extensions or lists which extensions match a type. Covers the most widely used web and media types.

percentageChangeCalculator.zeroBase: A percentage cannot be calculated because the starting value is zero.
percentageChangeCalculator.empty: Enter two numbers to compare them.
percentageChangeCalculator.tip: Percentage change equals (new - old) divided by |old| times 100. A positive result means an increase.

fuelEconomyCalculator.empty: Enter a consumption value and pick its unit.
fuelEconomyCalculator.tip: Compare the three common fuel economy measures: litres per 100 km, miles per US gallon and km per litre.

electricityCostCalculator.empty: Fill in all four fields to estimate your usage and cost.
electricityCostCalculator.tip: Consumption = watts divided by 1000 times hours times days. Multiply by your kWh price for the bill estimate.

caloriesBurnedCalculator.empty: Enter your weight and duration to see an estimate.
caloriesBurnedCalculator.tip: Uses the MET formula: kcal = MET times 3.5 times weight (kg) divided by 200 times minutes. Results are approximate.

imageCombiner.empty: Pick two images to combine them side by side.
imageCombiner.tip: Both images are drawn onto one canvas and downloaded as a single PNG. The result uses the taller of the two heights. Nothing is uploaded.

imageFlipper.empty: Pick an image and choose how to mirror it.
imageFlipper.tip: Mirrors your image left-right or top-bottom and downloads it as PNG. All processing is local.

sitemapUrlExtractor.placeholder: Paste the XML of your sitemap...
sitemapUrlExtractor.empty: Paste sitemap XML above to extract every URL.
sitemapUrlExtractor.tip: Extracts every loc value from your XML sitemap. Handy for bulk-checking indexed pages or building URL lists.

jokeGenerator.empty: Tap the button for a random programmer joke.
jokeGenerator.tip: A hand-picked set of programmer jokes shipped with the page. The button skips the current joke, so the next one is always fresh.

randomQuoteGenerator.empty: Tap the button for a random quote.
randomQuoteGenerator.tip: A curated set of quotes bundled in the page. Tap again for a new one; nothing leaves your device.

guessTheNumber.intro: I am thinking of a secret number between 1 and 100. Find it in as few guesses as you can.
guessTheNumber.low: Too low - try a bigger number.
guessTheNumber.high: Too high - try a smaller number.
guessTheNumber.empty: Type a number between 1 and 100, then press Guess.
guessTheNumber.tip: Every guess tells you whether the answer is higher or lower. The best strategy wins in at most 7 tries.
